claim: A critic agent that poses probing scientific questions challenging assumptions and focus guides simulations and experiments to target key mechanisms and outcomes.
falsifier: In a multi-agent scientific discovery system, introduce a critic agent that generates probing questions challenging assumptions and measure whether the resulting simulations and experiments more frequently target key mechanisms and outcomes compared to a system without such a critic.

conditions: the critic agent is integrated into a multi-agent system
the critic agent poses probing questions that challenge assumptions and focus
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, tasks, and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Critic agent posing probing for simulations and experiments target

claim: If a uniform non-adaptive quantum locally random reduction exists from a worst-case QMA-hard promise problem to the task of inverting a one-way permutation, then coQMA is contained in QIP(2).
falsifier: The conditional can be tested by attempting to construct the specified uniform non-adaptive quantum locally random reduction, or by proving that no such reduction can exist under the stated complexity assumptions.

conditions: the reduction is quantum locally random
the source problem is a worst-case QMA-hard promise problem
the target task is inverting a one-way permutation
exclusions: The implication holds within the standard formal model of quantum reductions and interactive proof systems; it is conditional on the stated existence assumptions and does not assert that such a reduction actually exists.

title: Complexity classes coQMA–inclusion of coQMA theorem
